newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen Daschle sees Clinton firm on tobacco rule.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen Daschle sees Clinton firm on tobacco rule.

text.p: Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle said Tuesday he expects President Clinton will remain committed to the regulation of tobacco even after the resignation of Food and Drug Administration chief David Kessler, who spearheaded the plan.

"I have no expectation whatsoever that the administration will roll back their proposals," the South Dakota Democrat told reporters. He said he knew personally of the president's commitment to the issue. "It was really an effort that was completely embraced by the Vice President, the President and everybody in the White House itself."
FDA Commissioner Kessler said he intended to remain on the job until a successor was found, which Daschle interpreted to mean until the Senate has confirmed a new commissioner.
"He will be here for some time if the Republicans or others would choose to oppose his successor," Daschle said.
The tobacco industry's legal challenge to proposed tough restrictions on tobacco advertising and other rules to curb teen smoking is pending in the courts.
